raw.description:
VOTING IS POWER. 🗳️🗽 Vote, Roll & Watch Party

This Election Day, let’s vote — then roll! (The last day to register to vote is Oct 24th)

Join us at Xanadu for Rolling for Democracy, a night of music, community and celebrating the power of every voice.

Wear your “I Voted” sticker for FREE admission, then skate, dance and follow this historic day together. We’ll have multiple TV screens tuned to different networks throughout the night.

🎶 Sounds by Misbehaviour, Varunisme, Silent H & Serrian

genre: 90's hip hop, house, soul

Presented by Rebecca Lynn / Vinyl Nights

Get your friends to vote, bring your sticker and come roll with us! ❤️

@dancingfordemocracy\_ is a non-partisan celebration of participation, community and the power of every voice.

Booth reservations are available for parties 7+ via form: https://www.xanadu.nyc/booking

General Admission tickets are included in all booth reservations.

🚨Important Info🚨

· Ticket does \*NOT\* include Skate Rental.

· Skates & safety gear are available to rent \*\*first come, first served\*\*

· All sales are final. No refunds.

· You must sign the Xanadu waiver in advance here: https://shorturl.at/AJbHn

· Valid Government ID required for entry. Photos of IDs are not accepted

· Gum, outside food and drink is not allowed.

· All bags are subject to search at the venue entrance.

· Xanadu is wheelchair accessible and includes entry ramps and ADA bathrooms. Write to info@xanadu.nyc if you require extra assistance.

· Xanadu is an inclusive, safe space. We do not tolerate harassment, aggression, racism, bigotry, or hatred of any kind.

Skating is FUN. Skating is RISKY!

Together we will create a skate experience that is fun and safe for everyone on the rink!

· Be mindful of yourself, your limits and others around you.

· Our Skate Guards are always here to help! Please alert them to any hazards or unsafe behavior on the rink so that they can help.

· Rink capacity fluctuates throughout each session- if you are ever feeling overwhelmed, take a quick break and get back into the flow when you’re ready.

· Keep each other safe & happy! Less friction, more FLOW.

More questions? Find answers here: xanadu.nyc/FAQ

✨By purchasing a ticket, you agree to and are bound by Xanadu's Terms and Conditions: https://tinyurl.com/XanaduTermsConditions

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.title: How old do I have to be to enter SILO?

value.body: SILO is a space for people to dance, to hear music, and to express themselves. While you are here, we want you to feel safe, comfortable, and at home. We do not tolerate violence, harassment, racism, homophobia, transphobia, or bigotry of any kind. We do not allow unwanted contact. This includes leering, staring, and cutting off someone else’s ability to move freely.
value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. Our staff is trained to assist you, so just give them a heads up when you arrive and they will make sure you’re able to get in. Reserved seating can be arranged by emailing a11y@silobrooklyn.com. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.
value.title: Transfer your ticket to a friend

value.title: Do you guys use haze/fog?

value.body: Earplugs are $2 at the front bar.

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Brutalismus 3000 headlines a special edition of RUSH alongside SPFDJ, Dorian Electra, Eera, and Nurse (Body Bag) on Nov 6.

The German duo has exploded onto the global stage with a singularly unhinged take on the rave-techno-hardcore continuum. Fusing gabber and schranz with hyperpop-worthy hooks and a sense of punk populism inherited from artists like The Prodigy, Brutalismus 3000 land like a sledgehammer against the stifling forces of conformity.

SPFDJ makes her long-awaited RUSH debut. The Herrensauna resident and Intrepid Skin label boss is one of the most notorious DJs working today. Her singular mix of raw, thundering techno, tweaked, wired club sounds, fearless rave moments and cheeky vocal flips has made her a figurehead for a generation of artists who dare to reimagine clubbing through a defiant, punk lens. Surf Gang's Eera is one of the driving forces behind the modern wave of hyper-blended electronic music, where trance, hardcore, emo and much more swirl together in a vivid tapestry.

Neo-pop diva Dorian Electra joins with a special DJ set. They arrive fresh off the release of their new self-titled LP, a run of covers that reimagines ten classic songs through a manic, high-speed filter. Finally, Body Bag affiliate Nurse ramps up the BPM to dangerous levels. The Body Bag tagline promises "grotesque hardcore" - Nurse delivers.

Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.

If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

three decades of uk soundsystem pressure bent into techno (dub dna, no nostalgia) then the italo-ebm bloodline answering back, dark and machine-driven. different decades, same spine.  
  
martyn: broken rhythms, bass weight and a detroit sensibility, always resisting a single lane. his long panorama bar residency became a key home for that approach, while 3024 pushed the same openness into his own label world. kendal: italo, ebm and early trance run through his work. with infravision, they called that collision “italo body music”, a harder, more futuristic take on those sounds. for kein klub, kendal takes it somewhere darker.

ksenyeah + manguito: ’26 has been a breakout year for both artists. on november 6, they return to kein klub to take over room 2, playing house for four hours.

On November 7th, Prunk brings PIV to H0L0 in Queens for a two stage takeover with Kellie Allen, MADVILLA, m.O.N.R.O.E., ARMII1N, Jayside, Bea Trinidad, Lauren Ritter, and Kiyoshi909. The main room features Prunk, Kellie Allen, MADVILLA, and m.O.N.R.O.E., while a second stage offers a more intimate way to hear some of New York’s local talent.

Founded by Prunk in 2015, PIV has grown from an Amsterdam house label into a respected international label, event series, and party brand. Inspired by the house sounds of New York and Chicago, PIV has hosted showcases at Tomorrowland Belgium, fabric London, Pacha Barcelona, Cova Santa, Amnesia Ibiza, and Shelter Amsterdam. PIV stands for People Invited, or VIP spelled backwards, reflecting the idea that house music is for everyone.

Prunk’s catalog includes releases on PIV, Defected, Djebali, Key Records, and Ewax, while his touring history spans Space Miami, Hï Ibiza, Awakenings, fabric, elrow, and The BPM Festival. Kellie Allen brings releases on PIV, Moxy Muzik, Dansu Discs, and Do Not Sleep while MADVILLA arrives after PIV Amsterdam appearances and Mixmag Lab London. m.O.N.R.O.E. adds releases on Get Physical, Saved Records, Desert Hearts, and Cuttin’ Headz. Together, the lineup brings the wider PIV family and New York’s local house community under one roof. From longtime label artists to new names in the city, this edition brings the sound and community surrounding PIV into two rooms for a full night inside one of Queens’ top clubs.

value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible for me t

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.
value.title: Transfer your ticket to a friend

raw.description:
***Xanadu Day Disco***

***Get ready for a magical, neon-bright celebration inspired by the legendary spirit of Xanadu! Join us for a glitter-filled daytime disco where music, movement, and imagination collide. Whether you’re 5 or 95, this all-ages event brings the joy of roller-disco vibes, dazzling colors, and feel-good energy.***

***Vibe and skate to the music of disco, house, pop***

***Booth reservations are available for parties 7+ via form: https://www.xanadu.nyc/booking***

***General Admission tickets are included in all booth reservations.***

🚨Important Info🚨

· Guests between 16 and 17 admitted with a skate waiver signed by a legal guardian. Guests under 16 admitted if accompanied by a legal guardian.

· Ticket does \*NOT\* include Skate Rental.

· Skates & safety gear are available to rent \*\*first come, first served\*\*

· All sales are final. No refunds.

· You must sign the Xanadu waiver in advance here: https://shorturl.at/AJbHn

· Valid Government ID required for entry. Photos of IDs are not accepted

· Gum, outside food and drink is not allowed.

· All bags are subject to search at the venue entrance.

· Xanadu is wheelchair accessible and includes entry ramps and ADA bathrooms. Write to info@xanadu.nyc if you require extra assistance.

· Xanadu is an inclusive, safe space. We do not tolerate harassment, aggression, racism, bigotry, or hatred of any kind.

Skating is FUN. Skating is RISKY!

Together we will create a skate experience that is fun and safe for everyone on the rink!

· Be mindful of yourself, your limits and others around you.

· Our Skate Guards are always here to help! Please alert them to any hazards or unsafe behavior on the rink so that they can help.

· Rink capacity fluctuates throughout each session- if you are ever feeling overwhelmed, take a quick break and get back into the flow when you’re ready.

· Keep each other safe & happy! Less friction, more FLOW.

More questions? Find answers here: xanadu.nyc/FAQ

✨By purchasing a ticket, you agree to and are bound by Xanadu's Terms and Conditions: https://tinyurl.com/XanaduTermsConditions

Honey Trap’s first roller disco night at Xanadu🛼 is finally happening on SUNDAY, November 8th at 8 PM

We are joined by New Orlean’s most dangerous gay Bouffant Bouffant and the Honey Trap residents Amelia Holt, Second Contact and Conduit.

Come for a little sweat and dance ;)

Mark your calendars!

A love letter to Sunday Skate Club 🫶

Every Sunday from 8–12am, the rink becomes more than a skate session. It’s a weekly ritual where local club kids, industry folks, and NYC’s DJs get their flowers — and skate heads and music heads move in the same orbit.

Here you see the true versatility of a DJ. That epic artist you loved at 5am now accepts the challenge of an all-skate set around a groovy 100bpm — R&B, disco, and other unexpected jams. It’s a rare chance to hear their non-unz unz selections like R&B, disco, you name it. From thudding foggy sweaty beats the morning before (well, it may have still been your ‘night’) to idyllic skating in a psychedelic rink with jams that make you smile big. You start with a few laps, feeling out the floor, the room fills, the rhythm builds, and before long, you’re moving without thinking — just you, the music, and the night.

Then you notice friends slipping into the bathrooms… only it’s Club Flush, pulling the off-wheels crowd into something sweatier, louder, a little unhinged. Red-lit and hazy, fog stretching the room so it feels bigger than it is. An 18” sub shakes the floor, a hidden 21” built straight into the booth hits your chest. There are no grimy stalls, no smells (thanks all!) just a fully enclosed, immersive room. A few minutes in, and you forget you’re even standing in a bathroom. You might walk in for a second and stay for half a set. You might discover your new favorite DJ. You might skate, then dance, then skate again. That’s the point.

Every week is a different crew, a different sound, a different pocket of the city’s underground stepping forward. Sunday Skate Club is about unified movement — wheels, feet, bass, community. When these scenes overlap, the energy multiplies, and the night becomes something bigger than the sum of its parts.

See you every Sunday at 8.

Cosmic Gate takes over Superior Ingredients Rooftop on Sunday, November 8, joined by Sinca, Derya Zor, sunrYse, and 4YÛ.

For more than 27 years, German artist Nic Chagall has built Cosmic Gate into one of trance’s most recognized names. His catalog includes genre classics “Fire Wire” and “Exploration of Space,” alongside fan favorites such as “am2pm,” “Fall Into You,” “Nothing To Hide,” and “Your Mind.”

GRAMMY-nominated and once named the highest climber in DJ Mag’s Top 100, Cosmic Gate has performed at Tomorrowland, EDC, Ultra, Creamfields, Dreamstate, Transmission, and A State of Trance. His remix catalog includes music from Armin van Buuren, Tiësto, deadmau5, Above & Beyond, and Gabriel & Dresden. He also runs Wake Your Mind Records and hosts the weekly WYM Radio show.

Joining him is Montréal DJ and producer Sinca, whose sets move between progressive house, classic house, minimal, and indie dance. Her music has appeared on Purified, Bedrock, Anjunadeep, All Day I Dream, and Days Like Nights, with performances at Coachella’s Do LaB, Burning Man, SXM Festival, Stereo Montréal, Brooklyn Mirage, and Akasha Ibiza.

Local artists Derya Zor, sunrYse, and 4YÛ complete the lineup for a Sunday above Brooklyn.

value.title: Can I bring my own food and drink?

value.body:
We have lockers available for rental, as well as various hooks and cubbies around the space.

value.title: Where can I put my stuff?

value.body:
There is no smoke or e-smoke permitted in the venue.

There is a designated outdoor smoking area during select evenings.
value.title: Can I smoke indoors?

value.body:
We are a 21+ venue unless otherwise stated. Please check the event description on Dice to verify the age requirement for the event you’re interested in.

All shows require a valid government-issued photo ID or passport to enter. The ID must be issued by the commissioner of motor vehicles, federal government, any United States territory, commonwealth or possession, the District of Columbia, a state government within the United States or a provincial government of the dominion of Canada. Alternatively, a valid passport issued by the United States government or any other country can be used. We DO NOT accept any photographs of IDs or passports, nor do we accept expired IDs. If necessary, we may request a second form of ID.

For events that are 16+ or 18+, all under age guests must be accompanied by a legal guardian, and both parties must have tickets and a physical photo ID.
value.title: Are there age restrictions or an ID policy?

value.body:
All Ticket Sales Are Final: This means that once you purchase a ticket, it is non-refundable unless the event is canceled or rescheduled by the event organizer.

Event Details Are Subject to Change: Event details such as the lineup, start time, set times, and stage may change without prior notice. These changes can occur due to circumstances beyond our control.

Postponement: If an event is rescheduled ticket-holders typically have two options:

Option (a): Keep their ticket, which will be honored at the rescheduled date.

Option (b): Request a refund within 7 dates of the event being rescheduled.

Full Cancellation: If an event is canceled entirely, ticket refunds will be processed automatically. However, it may take up to 7 business days for the refund to be processed.
value.title: What is your refund policy?

value.body: We are only open on an events basis, please refer to our calendar for our full list of skate sessions, live shows, and club nights.
value.title: Can I come in for free/no cover?

value.body: We do not offer valet parking nor do we have a parking lot, but there is street parking located around the venue.
value.title: Is there parking?

value.body: General admission guarantees entry to the venue.
value.title: What is included in a general admission ticket?

value.body: On Xanadu Club Night, there is a skate session from 7-10pm. At 10pm, the rink closes for skating and opens for dancing.
value.title: How does Xanadu Club Night work?

value.body:
The majority of our live events are not skating events. Sometimes we have skate sessions with live music accompaniment, but that would be explicitly stated in the event details.

We have pre-show skate sessions prior to most of our non-skating live shows from 6-8pm.
value.title: Can I skate during live shows?

value.body:
We welcome all bodies in our space. All entrances and spaces within the venue are single-level and there is a wheelchair / mobility aid accessible ramp at the main entrance. Strobe lights may be used during performances and parties.

Please email info@xanadu.nyc when you purchase a ticket for a Xanadu event to discuss your needs and ensure proper accommodations.
value.title: Are there ADA accommodations?

value.body:
We require waivers for entry into the building whenever skating is happening. If you have completed a digital waiver within the last 12 months, there is no need to complete another. You can fill out your waiver ahead of time at bit.ly/4iQPmHd  
  
We do not require a waiver for no-skate, shoes-only events such as club nights and some live shows.

**🛼 About Sunday Afterglow: (skate)🛼**

**Ease into the end of the weekend with a mellow, magical skating session designed for everyone — kids, teens, adults, families, and first-time skaters. Sunday Afterglow blends chill music, soft lights, and easygoing energy to help you unwind, connect, and roll into a brand-new week feeling refreshed.**

**Vibe and skate to the music of disco, house, pop**

**Booth reservations are available for parties 7+ via form: https://www.xanadu.nyc/booking**

**General Admission tickets are included in all booth reservations.**

**🚨Important Info🚨**

· Guests between 16 and 17 admitted with a skate waiver signed by a legal guardian. Guests under 16 admitted if accompanied by a legal guardian.

· Ticket does \*NOT\* include Skate Rental.

· Skates & safety gear are available to rent \*\*first come, first served\*\*

· All sales are final. No refunds.

· You must sign the Xanadu waiver in advance here: https://shorturl.at/AJbHn

· Valid Government ID required for entry. Photos of IDs are not accepted

· Gum, outside food and drink is not allowed.

· All bags are subject to search at the venue entrance.

· Xanadu is wheelchair accessible and includes entry ramps and ADA bathrooms. Write to info@xanadu.nyc if you require extra assistance.

· Xanadu is an inclusive, safe space. We do not tolerate harassment, aggression, racism, bigotry, or hatred of any kind.

**Skating is FUN. Skating is RISKY!**

Together we will create a skate experience that is fun and safe for everyone on the rink!

· Be mindful of yourself, your limits and others around you.

· Our Skate Guards are always here to help! Please alert them to any hazards or unsafe behavior on the rink so that they can help.

· Rink capacity fluctuates throughout each session- if you are ever feeling overwhelmed, take a quick break and get back into the flow when you’re ready.

· Keep each other safe & happy! Less friction, more FLOW.

More questions? Find answers here: xanadu.nyc/FAQ

✨By purchasing a ticket, you agree to and are bound by Xanadu's Terms and Conditions: https://tinyurl.com/XanaduTermsConditions

raw.description:
SONIDO DE BOGOTÁ IS A DEDICATION TO THE CITY AND THE ELECTRONIC MUSIC CULTURE THAT CONTINUES TO SHAPE OUR IDENTITY. THIS SPECIAL EDITION BRINGS TO NEW YORK A SELECTION OF ARTISTS REPRESENTING DIFFERENT GENERATIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS OF BOGOTÁ’S TECHNO SOUND. A REFLECTION OF THE MUSIC, THE SPACES AND THE PEOPLE THAT HAVE MADE THE CITY AN ESSENTIAL PART OF OUR HISTORY.

BORN IN NEW YORK, ROOTED IN BOGOTÁ, CRUD0 WAS FOUNDED ON AN UNDERSTANDING OF TECHNO AS MORE THAN ENTERTAINMENT, A DISCIPLINE AND A COLLECTIVE EXPERIENCE CENTERED ON THE DANCE FLOOR. OVER DECADES, BOGOTÁ HAS DEVELOPED A DISTINCT MUSICAL LANGUAGE THROUGH EXPERIMENTATION, INDEPENDENCE AND A RESISTANCE TO COMMERCIAL CONVENTIONS. A SCENE BUILT ON ITS OWN TERMS, WITHOUT COMPROMISING ITS ORIGINAL VISION.

THIS PHILOSOPHY REMAINS CENTRAL TO CRUD0, INFORMING ITS CURATORIAL DIRECTION AND ITS COMMITMENT TO LONG HOURS, UNCOMPROMISING SOUND AND A PROTECTED DANCE FLOOR.

SELECTORS

PAULA VÉLEZ

A TRUE REPRESENTATIVE OF BOGOTÁ’S TECHNO SOUND, PAULA VÉLEZ HAS BEEN AN ACTIVE FORCE IN COLOMBIA’S ELECTRONIC MUSIC SCENE SINCE 2005. HER JOURNEY BEGAN WITH ACID COMMANDERS, A FOUR-TURNTABLE ACID TECHNO PROJECT THAT SHAPED HER DEEP CONNECTION TO VINYL AND THE RAW FOUNDATIONS OF THE GENRE.

IN 2008, SHE LAUNCHED HER SOLO PROJECT, CITRIK POLLY, EXPLORING NEW DIMENSIONS OF TECHNO WHILE ESTABLISHING BULLET, A FEMALE DJ COLLECTIVE AND EVENT PLATFORM. HER WORK EXTENDED INTO VENEZUELA AND LATER EUROPE, WHERE SHE BECAME INVOLVED WITH MADRID’S KILLSOUND COLLECTIVE AND MELTING POT RECORDS, PERFORMING ACROSS SPAIN AND BERLIN.

AFTER FOUR YEARS IN EUROPE, PAULA RETURNED TO COLOMBIA, PERFORMING AT BAUM, TATACOA FESTIVAL, BLACK BOX FESTIVAL AND RADIKAL STYLES, WHILE REMAINING CONNECTED TO KEY PLATFORMS SUCH AS THC, BOGOTRAX AND INDUSTRIAL GIRLS. HER INTERNATIONAL JOURNEY ALSO INCLUDES NEW YORK, BOSTON, ECUADOR AND COSTA RICA.

WITH TWO DECADES BEHIND THE DECKS, PAULA VÉLEZ REMAINS A DISTINCTIVE REPRESENTATIVE OF COLOMBIAN TECHNO AND ITS ROOTS.

VARJU

BORN IN BOGOTÁ, VARJU REPRESENTS THE CURRENT IDENTITY OF THE CITY’S TECHNO SOUND. INFLUENCED BY THE RAW ENERGY OF ROCK AND METAL, HIS MUSICAL APPROACH MOVES THROUGH HYPNOTIC, MENTAL, ATMOSPHERIC AND RAW TECHNO, BUILT ON DEEP GROOVES, SUBTLE MELODIC PROGRESSIONS AND PRECISE RHYTHMIC STRUCTURES. HIS DJ SETS GO BEYOND CONVENTIONAL MIXING, DEVELOPING CAREFULLY CONSTRUCTED NARRATIVES THROUGH TENSION, MOVEMENT AND SONIC EXPLORATION.

AS A PRODUCER, VARJU CONTINUES TO DEVELOP HIS OWN SONIC IDENTITY, EXPLORING THE BOUNDARIES BETWEEN TECHNO AND EXPERIMENTAL ELECTRONIC MUSIC. BEYOND THE BOOTH, HE PLAYS AN ACTIVE ROLE IN BOGOTÁ’S ELECTRONIC MUSIC CULTURE THROUGH HIS WORK WITH GRV.DVSN AND BAUM BOGOTÁ.

HIS JOURNEY HAS LED HIM TO SHARE THE STAGE WITH ARTISTS SUCH AS OSCAR MULERO, ADRIANA LOPEZ, THE ADVENT, CLAUDIO PRC, TOMMY FOUR SEVEN, PETER VAN HOESEN, RENE WISE, TEMUDO AND QUELZA, ESTABLISHING HIM AS PART OF A GENERATION SHAPING THE PRESENT AND FUTURE OF COLOMBIAN TECHNO.

GIOVANI

EMERGING FROM BOGOTÁ’S FORMATIVE YEARS OF ELECTRONIC MUSIC, GIOVANI BELONGS TO A GENERATION OF ARTISTS WHO HELPED ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATIONS OF THE CITY’S TECHNO CULTURE. ACTIVE SINCE 2000, HIS EARLY YEARS WERE SHAPED BY A GROWING NETWORK OF INDEPENDENT CLUBS AND DANCE FLOORS. IN 2003, VICTORIES AT THE HUMAN PATTERN AND THE RIDDLE DJ CONTESTS LED TO HIS FIRST RESIDENCY AT SUBROYAL, A KEY CHAPTER IN HIS DEVELOPMENT BEHIND THE DECKS.

DRAWING FROM ELECTRO, TECHNO, HOUSE AND BREAKS, HIS SELECTIONS REFLECTED THE MUSICAL DIVERSITY OF BOGOTÁ’S EARLY ELECTRONIC MOVEMENT. THROUGH APPEARANCES AT MONITOR, BARBARELLA, ARENA, LA SALA AND 4ROOMS, GIOVANI BECAME PART OF A CLUB CULTURE THAT WOULD CONTINUE TO DEFINE THE CITY’S ELECTRONIC MUSIC IDENTITY.

WITH OVER TWO DECADES BEHIND THE DECKS, GIOVANI REMAINS A DIRECT CONNECTION BETWEEN BOGOTÁ’S TECHNO ROOTS AND NEW YORK’S DANCE FLOORS.

Club Cocoa is an emerging queer party series founded by NYC-based Nigerian artist halima - built for the diaspora, by the diaspora.

A call out to the queer African babes, Club Cocoa is a meeting point for the pan-African where legacy lands on the dance floor. Inspired by the spirit of Lagos’ Festac 77 festival, Club Cocoa functions as a remembrance of a culture where we dream and build together.

That Afro-future our predecessors were striving for, we’re reimagining here.

Hurry. Club Cocoa is calling…

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Harvey needs no introduction - he is one of dance music's true rockstars, with a career that spans from the mid-80s through a legendary Ministry of Sound residency, through the early '00s when he was a figurehead in the disco renaissance through today. Paying homage to a lineage of Black innovators while forging her own path, Diggs has infused the genre with new life.

We welcome all bodies in our space. All entrances and spaces within the venue are single-level and there is a wheelchair / mobility aid accessible ramp at the main entrance. Strobe lights may be used during performances and parties.

Please email info@xanadu.nyc when you purchase a ticket for a Xanadu event to discuss your needs and ensure proper accommodations.
value.title: Are there ADA accommodations?

value.body:
We require waivers for entry into the building whenever skating is happening. If you have completed a digital waiver within the last 12 months, there is no need to complete another. You can fill out your waiver ahead of time at bit.ly/4iQPmHd  
  
We do not require a waiver for no-skate, shoes-only events such as club nights and some live shows.

Founded in New York in 1991, Nervous Records has been a constant presence in the evolution of house music culture for over three decades. Emerging from the city’s club underground and growing into a globally recognized label, Nervous has maintained a strong sense of identity while adapting to shifting scenes, formats, and audiences The company is currently America's Longest Standing Dance Brand. Having started with releases from Louie Vega, Todd Terry, Kenny Dope and Roger Sanchez, Nervous has continued throughout its 35 year existence to be a source of many of the world's most memorable dancefloor bombs. Just recently Nervous released worldwide anthems from Mau P ("The Less I Know The Better), Mochakk ("Da Fonk Feat. Joni") and Loofy ("Last Night.) In addition to the music, Nervous Records has a highly innovative merchandise line that highlights its universally recognized Cartoon Logo, and an active Event Promotion Team that produces and curates some of the most memorable DJ events in its homebase of New York.

With The Nervous Records X The Crown Emerging DJ Showcase, Nervous is partnering with one of downtown Manhattan's buzziest venues with a premier sound system and spectacular "Only In New York" Skyline View to create an excellent platform for new talent to shine for a well-informed and enthusiastic club audience.

On Saturday, November 14th, Cadence welcomes UK producer Seb Wildblood to a secret loft in the heart of Lower Manhattan for a night of rhythm, melody, and something a little stranger than usual.

**THE LINEUP**

Seb Wildblood (UK) - London underground legend - bringing together woozy, soulful synths for the dance floor, with melodies that hit harder than you expect. He's the founder of the early 2010's Church party in South London and the 'All My Thoughts' label. Expect trippy, percussive, and unbelievably danceable grooves.

Delacour (NYC) - One of the best of the best in current NYC talent. Delacour's tracks combine the deepest rhythms with moving melodic undertones. Releases span Deeperfect, Andhera, and recent EP 'In Your Atmosphere.'

Elkind B3B Hugh Zhang B3B RYô - Cadence resident triple threat. We'll be teleporting you away from Manhattan into Jupiter. Or Mars.

Pancho B2B J2 - Setting the tone from the jump.

**THE THEME: THE GREENHOUSE**

This time, we're introducing a new theme to the party: the greenhouse. Take that however you want, but we're turning the loft into a strange little garden after dark.

**ABOUT CADENCE**

2026 has been a year of venturing into the unknown for us, leaning into a newer Balearic sound that's heavy on nostalgia and groove. But as many of you know, we started DIY, and we can't wait to show you what we have in store.

**LOCATION**

Secret loft location, Lower Manhattan (address will be shared with ticket holders day-of show)

Cadence is a space for everyone. We welcome people of all genders, races, sexualities, and backgrounds, and we're committed to keeping the dance floor safe and respectful for all.

Discrimination, harassment, or aggressive behavior of any kind will not be tolerated. Anyone acting against the spirit of the party will be asked to leave.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

With over two decades of electronic music eminence, Eli Escobar has confirmed his place amongst dance music greats. With an unparalleled record collection of handpicked gems and curveball productions, Escobar guides revellers through the heartbeat of music, from the past to the future.

Always looking forward and keeping step with evolving generational tastes, Escobar has redefined his sound in recent years. As an acquainted DJ & Producer, the dance music veteran cut his teeth into the epicentre of 1990’s New York City hedonism and set the foundations for an admirable career. Releasing music on influential labels such as Phonica, Razor n Tape, Defected’s ‘Classic’ and his very own label imprint Night People, only gives a snapshot into the depth of his discovery.

Spanning over more than 20 years, the influence and presence of Eli Escobar is undeniable in every corner of dance music. As a selector he has appeared on a variety of influential platforms including BBC Radio 1 Essential Mix, Resident Advisor's Exchange Podcast, Boiler Room, Mixmag ‘The Lab’ and The Lot Radio, only to name a few. Likewise transporting his sound to dancefloors across the world with residencies at House of Yes, Le Bain, Battlehymn and beyond.

Globally respected and recognised as a forward thinking producer, Escobar’s output steps beyond conventional dance music with remix work for the likes of Lana Del Rey, M.I.A., Honey Dijon, Cakes Da Killa and many more. Now heading into 2023 Eli looks to stay true to his musical progression.

\--
  
Bag Raiders are icons of the Australian dance scene. After dropping cult underground cuts (Fun Punch, Turbo Love, Big Fun), Jack Glass and Chris Stracey signed to Modular Records and released their game-changing, self-titled debut album in 2010, debuting at No. 7 on the ARIA Album Chart and earning nominations from ARIA, triple j and APRA. The LP featured hit singles Way Back Home, Sunlight, Snake Charmer, and the now-legendary Shooting Stars — one of the biggest Australian dance tracks of all time. Shooting Stars has become a global phenomenon, racking up over 4 billion streams, 40+ Platinum and 7 Gold certifications, 18 million Shazams and peaked at No. 11 on Billboard’s Dance chart.

They followed with acclaimed EPs (Waterfalls, Checkmate, Friend Inside) and teamed up with Mayer Hawthorne on Beat Me to the Punch. Their second LP Horizons arrived in 2019, followed by the launch of their label Broken Head Records in 2022 and club-driven releases like Love Me Back and Right Here / Saliba.

In 2023, Troye Sivan sampled Shooting Stars on his Grammy-nominated single Got Me Started, and they dropped collabs with Boston Bun (SAVE ME) and Panama (Flowers).

In 2025 and beyond, Bag Raiders are locked in for a relentless release schedule of club weapons — kicking off with Hold Me, out now on UK label The Cross Records.

On Saturday, November 14th, Cadence welcomes UK producer Seb Wildblood to a secret loft in the heart of Lower Manhattan for a night of rhythm, melody, and something a little stranger than usual.

**THE LINEUP**

Seb Wildblood (UK) - London underground legend - bringing together woozy, soulful synths for the dance floor, with melodies that hit harder than you expect. He's the founder of the early 2010's Church party in South London and the 'All My Thoughts' label. Expect trippy, percussive, and unbelievably danceable grooves.

Delacour (NYC) - One of the best of the best in current NYC talent. Delacour's tracks combine the deepest rhythms with moving melodic undertones. Releases span Deeperfect, Andhera, and recent EP 'In Your Atmosphere.'

Elkind B3B Hugh Zhang B3B RYô - Cadence resident triple threat. We'll be teleporting you away from Manhattan into Jupiter. Or Mars.

Pancho B2B J2 - Setting the tone from the jump.

**THE THEME: THE GREENHOUSE**

This time, we're introducing a new theme to the party: the greenhouse. Take that however you want, but we're turning the loft into a strange little garden after dark.

**ABOUT CADENCE**

2026 has been a year of venturing into the unknown for us, leaning into a newer Balearic sound that's heavy on nostalgia and groove. But as many of you know, we started DIY, and we can't wait to show you what we have in store.

**LOCATION**

Secret loft location, Lower Manhattan (address will be shared with ticket holders day-of show)

**ENTRY & HOUSE POLICY**

Cadence is a space for everyone. We welcome people of all genders, races, sexualities, and backgrounds, and we're committed to keeping the dance floor safe and respectful for all.

Discrimination, harassment, or aggressive behavior of any kind will not be tolerated. Anyone acting against the spirit of the party will be asked to leave.

This DURATIONS Sunday is all about dub its trajectories. Shaped by a life lived across key musical landscapes, Ayanna Heaven’s sets are historically-rooted yet forward-looking. K Wata’s live set draws from *Give U Space*: its bassbin minimalism and psychoacoustic precision. Ghost Dubs comes next, sending the further-submerged rhythms of his recent dub techno abstraction *Oblique*. Yu Su closes the festival. Her sonic evolution and newfound taste for the dancefloor moves slowly and builds gradually, always with restraint — however strange.

DURATIONS Festival is a week-long, multi-disciplinary exploration of sound and connection. Now in its fifth iteration, the festival’s programming is its most robust yet, with seven days of music, talks, audiovisual work taking place between Public Records, Pioneer Works, Roulette, and Whitney Museum of American Art.

To share feedback about an incident, please email hello@publicrecords.nyc or alert a member of our team.

raw.description:
Sunday Skate Club ft. Sissies of Mercy | Club Flush: Sidestreets (skate)

A love letter to Sunday Skate Club 🫶

Every Sunday from 8–12am, the rink becomes more than a skate session. It’s a weekly ritual where local club kids, industry folks, and NYC’s DJs get their flowers — and skate heads and music heads move in the same orbit.

Here you see the true versatility of a DJ. That epic artist you loved at 5am now accepts the challenge of an all-skate set around a groovy 100bpm — R&B, disco, and other unexpected jams. It’s a rare chance to hear their non-unz unz selections like R&B, disco, you name it. From thudding foggy sweaty beats the morning before (well, it may have still been your ‘night’) to idyllic skating in a psychedelic rink with jams that make you smile big. You start with a few laps, feeling out the floor, the room fills, the rhythm builds, and before long, you’re moving without thinking — just you, the music, and the night.

Then you notice friends slipping into the bathrooms… only it’s Club Flush, pulling the off-wheels crowd into something sweatier, louder, a little unhinged. Red-lit and hazy, fog stretching the room so it feels bigger than it is. An 18” sub shakes the floor, a hidden 21” built straight into the booth hits your chest. There are no grimy stalls, no smells (thanks all!) just a fully enclosed, immersive room. A few minutes in, and you forget you’re even standing in a bathroom. You might walk in for a second and stay for half a set. You might discover your new favorite DJ. You might skate, then dance, then skate again. That’s the point.

Every week is a different crew, a different sound, a different pocket of the city’s underground stepping forward. Sunday Skate Club is about unified movement — wheels, feet, bass, community. When these scenes overlap, the energy multiplies, and the night becomes something bigger than the sum of its parts.

See you every Sunday at 8.

Vibe and skate to the music of 70s/80s Disco, Funk, R&B, and 90s/2000s Hip Hop

Booth reservations are available for parties 7+ via form: https://www.xanadu.nyc/booking

General Admission tickets are included in all booth reservations.

🚨Important Info🚨

· Ticket does \*NOT\* include Skate Rental.

· Skates & safety gear are available to rent \*\*first come, first served\*\*

· All sales are final. No refunds.

· You must sign the Xanadu waiver in advance here: https://shorturl.at/AJbHn

· Valid Government ID required for entry. Photos of IDs are not accepted

· Gum, outside food and drink is not allowed.

· All bags are subject to search at the venue entrance.

· Xanadu is wheelchair accessible and includes entry ramps and ADA bathrooms. Write to info@xanadu.nyc if you require extra assistance.

· Xanadu is an inclusive, safe space. We do not tolerate harassment, aggression, racism, bigotry, or hatred of any kind.

Skating is FUN. Skating is RISKY!

Together we will create a skate experience that is fun and safe for everyone on the rink!

· Be mindful of yourself, your limits and others around you.

· Our Skate Guards are always here to help! Please alert them to any hazards or unsafe behavior on the rink so that they can help.

· Rink capacity fluctuates throughout each session- if you are ever feeling overwhelmed, take a quick break and get back into the flow when you’re ready.

· Keep each other safe & happy! Less friction, more FLOW.

More questions? Find answers here: xanadu.nyc/FAQ

value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. raw.description:
Hosted by DJ and musician Steen, Open Decks is a creative and fun space where DJs can hang and share their house and techno music live. Hear your favorite or original tracks on Silo's front room sound system, a custom 15,000 watt Danley powerhouse.

If you want to play, talk to Steen to sign up. Sign-up is in person at the event only, slots are 12 minutes.

The first 3 DJ's play first-come-first-spin. Then we'll select names randomly from the sign-up list throughout the night, with extra weighting for DJs who arrive earlier. You'll get a half hour notice before your set time. This is to ensure that DJ's who can't make the initial sign up right at 8pm still get a chance to play.

This week's co-host is Remniqe and this open decks will double as a release party for their new EP: Iconic Demonic. Remniqe will play through the EP during their open decks set.

**Iconic Demonic**

Songs: Being Kind Is Sexy, Altercation, Iconic Demonic, In The Dark (Can’t See Me) ft. Cherry

Artist(s): Remniqe Ft. Cherry

Release Date: November 20th, 2026

Beatport Exclusive Date: November 6th, 2026

Iconic Demonic is an EP highlighting Remniqe’s dark and industrial side of production with four powerful Techno tracks with original vocals from Remniqe and Cherry. Musically and lyrically, the EP explores the conflicting and overlapping way that queer people are often viewed, both as figureheads of style and culture, and harbingers of societal decay. As Remniqe puts it, the music feels equally appropriate “on the runway or in the pit of hell.”

Free with advance RSVP. Question? Hit up your host on IG @steenschmidt

In SILO's front room. Limited capacity.

value.body: SILO is a space for people to dance, to hear music, and to express themselves. While you are here, we want you to feel safe, comfortable, and at home. We do not tolerate violence, harassment, racism, homophobia, transphobia, or bigotry of any kind. We do not allow unwanted contact. This includes leering, staring, and cutting off someone else’s ability to move freely.
value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. Our staff is trained to assist you, so just give them a heads up when you arrive and they will make sure you’re able to get in. Reserved seating can be arranged by emailing a11y@silobrooklyn.com. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible for me?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

His cutting edge, high-energy basslines, and masterwork song structures stimulate the senses, complimented by 100% original artwork that ties his unmistakable branding together under his DJ & Producer alias, Eptic.

At an early age Eptic found not only a love for Rock & Metal, but Drum & Bass – the inspiration behind him wanting to learn and produce himself at a mere fourteen years old. Laying the creative fundamentals down at such a young age has paved the way for the now well-known international bass enthusiast, gaining the respect and attention from, and ultimately collaborating with, many well known artists such as DJ Snake, Marshmello, Dillon Francis, Jauz, Juicy J, among others.

Equally known for both his music, off-stage comedy skits, and social media personality, Eptic has secured acclaim far outreaching the bass music community proving there’s no boundaries for the Eptic moniker. With the debut of his fabled “Overlord Stage” at the end of 2021, Bella gave us a thrilling glimpse of what’s in store for 2022.

Named after the 1920’s arts organization founded by Katherine Dreier, Man Ray and Marcel Duchamp, Société Anonyme is a pioneering members-only organization dedicated to exploring unconventional modes of self-expression. COME AS YOU ARE. DANCE AS YOU FEEL. ROLL INTO SOMETHING FABULOUS! 💖🏳️‍⚧️

We're turning up the love, the music & the disco drag spirit for TRANS FAMILY DISCO! ALL LOVE. ALL COLORS. ALL IDENTITIES. ONE BIG DISCO FAMILY!

Nov 20th is Transgender Day of Remembrance - we honor our trans siblings & those lost to anti- transgender violence. This night is about offering care on the day after - bringing us all together in a room and offering connections to local non-profits for care onsite.

This event is in partnership with What Will I Become - a documentary about trans boys, mental health & imagining a way forward. Exploring universal themes on mental health, grief and masculinity - What Will I Become? asks what to do with our community's collective heartbreak and honor that trans people are always more than their deaths. The film is directed by Lexie Bean & Logan Rozos. Check out their website for resources and info https://www.wwibdoc.com/ & watch the trailer here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ni2OOrQ4VZQ&t=31s (Follow them on IG @whatwillibecome\_doc/)

This is an invitation to bring the glitter, the life-affirming glamour, the sequins & your most fabulous disco look for a chance to win skates from IMPALA! DRESS DISCO & WIN SKATES!

Special Skate Lesson at 7:30pm in the middle of the rink with Lexie Bean.

Vinyl Nights at Xanadu is the ultimate throwback to the Golden Era of NYC roller skating — celebrating the music, style, energy and culture that ruled New York’s legendary rinks from the 1970s through the 1990s.

This isn’t just a roller party. It’s a celebration of NYC roller culture — past, present & future & the ways in which queer life has always been a part of it.

DJs

DJ Misbehaviour - London Born Brooklynite legend who went Viral with over 27 Millions Views spinning 90's Hip Hop records.

Illexxxandra - is a Brooklyn-based DJ and producer known for her high-energy blend of disco, funk, global bass, jungle, and underground dance music.

Tipyourdj - is a NYC nightlife DJ known for his provocative, unexpected sounds and dynamic sets across Brooklyn’s vibrant LGBTQ+ party scene.

Presented by Rebecca Lynn - Party Girl, Native New Yorker, Event Producer & Disco Queen

raw.description:
Joshwa returns to New York City on November 21 to celebrate his birthday with a special Open to Close set at Brooklyn staple 99 Scott. From 10 PM to 4 AM, the UK-born DJ and producer takes control of the room for six uninterrupted hours of his signature blend of house, UK garage, and rolling low-end grooves.

Fresh off appearances at Countdown Festival, Fisher's Catch & Release Takeover, Paradise Ibiza, and Night Trip, Joshwa continues to establish himself as one of the most in-demand names in club culture. Before the sold-out shows and festival stages, he taught himself production through YouTube tutorials, saved up for his first CDJs, and balanced music with dreams of becoming a professional footballer.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Sunday Skate Club ft. DJ Dream, Conrad Dirty Finger | Club Flush: Zariya & Mantle (skate)

A love letter to Sunday Skate Club 🫶

Every Sunday from 8–12am, the rink becomes more than a skate session. It’s a weekly ritual where local club kids, industry folks, and NYC’s DJs get their flowers — and skate heads and music heads move in the same orbit.

Here you see the true versatility of a DJ. That epic artist you loved at 5am now accepts the challenge of an all-skate set around a groovy 100bpm — R&B, disco, and other unexpected jams. It’s a rare chance to hear their non-unz unz selections like R&B, disco, you name it. From thudding foggy sweaty beats the morning before (well, it may have still been your ‘night’) to idyllic skating in a psychedelic rink with jams that make you smile big. You start with a few laps, feeling out the floor, the room fills, the rhythm builds, and before long, you’re moving without thinking — just you, the music, and the night.

Then you notice friends slipping into the bathrooms… only it’s Club Flush, pulling the off-wheels crowd into something sweatier, louder, a little unhinged. Red-lit and hazy, fog stretching the room so it feels bigger than it is. An 18” sub shakes the floor, a hidden 21” built straight into the booth hits your chest. There are no grimy stalls, no smells (thanks all!) just a fully enclosed, immersive room. A few minutes in, and you forget you’re even standing in a bathroom. You might walk in for a second and stay for half a set. You might discover your new favorite DJ. You might skate, then dance, then skate again. That’s the point.

Every week is a different crew, a different sound, a different pocket of the city’s underground stepping forward. Sunday Skate Club is about unified movement — wheels, feet, bass, community. When these scenes overlap, the energy multiplies, and the night becomes something bigger than the sum of its parts.

See you every Sunday at 8.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.

Then we'll transition to the usual open decks format with turntables in addition to CDJs for folks who want to spin vinyl.

Free with advance RSVP. Question? Hit up your host on IG @steenschmidt

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Caracas-born DJ and producer Tony Guerra was raised inside the rhythm. Surrounded from an early age by a family of promoters, percussionists, and club selectors, he quickly channeled that musical foundation into electronic music, taking cues from the minimal precision of Ricardo Villalobos and the soulful bounce of classic house heavyweights like Dennis Ferrer and Sandy Rivera.

After breaking out on Caracas's Hot 94 FM and co-founding the influential underground collective The Deep Party, Guerra turned his focus to production, blending raw tech grooves with Afro-Caribbean percussion. With early releases spanning imprints like Fat Line Music and Road Trip Recordings alongside regular international radio appearances, Guerra has established himself as a fixture of the South American circuit, continually taking his rhythm-forward sound to premier clubs and international dancefloors.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Space 92 returns to 99 Scott on Saturday, November 28, bringing his high-impact strain of techno back to Brooklyn for a late-night warehouse session with Gray Area.

The French producer has become one of the defining names in peak-time techno, ranking as Beatport’s best-selling Techno Peak Time/Drive artist since 2020 and earning a string of No. 1 records along the way. His sound pulls together trance-charged techno, distorted percussion, acid and flashes of nostalgia inspired by his love of vintage ‘80s sci-fi. His catalog stretches across Drumcode, Filth on Acid, Factory 93 and Arcane, with collaborations alongside Hardwell, HI-LO and Reinier Zonneveld. Remixes for Nicole Moudaber and Layton Giordani have also topped Beatport’s charts.

His latest run keeps that momentum moving with “Proton” alongside Alignment, a remix of Oxia’s “Domino,” “Dimension” on his TAKEOFF imprint and “Free My Soul” with Vini Vici and CERES. Beyond his solo work, Space 92 has joined POPOF for Turbulences, performing together on major festival stages around the world.

Now he returns to 99 Scott, where towering ceilings, exposed brick and an industrial main room set the stage for the kind of heavy, late-night session his music demands. Space 92 has played the Brooklyn warehouse before, and on November 28, he’s coming back for another round.

Tickets are limited. Secure yours and meet us on the dance floor Expect pressure, sci-fi atmosphere and a set built for late-night Brooklyn.

See you 99 Scott.

raw.description:
*Heavy Debt* is the debut solo album from Shane Butler, best known for work with his projects Olden Yolk and Quilt. Marking his first release since Olden Yolk’s 2019 album Living Theatre, the album refines the art-leaning folk of Butler’s past projects into a sharp, singular vision. While retaining many of the neo-psychedelic qualities of Butler's past work, Heavy Debt occupies a more grounded terrain—establishing a firm sonic and lyrical footing in a candid world entirely his own. Recorded in New York during the winter of 2025 alongside producer and multi instrumentalist Jon Nellen, the album pairs rapidly picked guitars and effected woodwinds (played by Isaiah Barr of experimental jazz troupe Onyx Collective) with rich, varied percussion. These calibrated arrangements anchor Butler’s playful lyrics, weaving semi-autobiographical stories about the vagaries of modern life with a plainspoken clarity and a dreamlike fiction.

Silk Fence is a New York–based instrumental electro-acoustic trio between three longtime friends and collaborators—Arian Shafiee (Guerilla Toss, etc.) on electric guitar, Booker Stardrum (SML, etc.) on drums and percussion, and Justin Frye (PC Worship, etc.) on double bass and tapes. The group stretches the sonic possibilities of their instruments while exploring long-form, texture-driven minimalism and time-based improvisation.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
As G-House powers forward at a menacing pace, BIJOU is the name on everyone’s lips. Instead of setting the bar for the genre, he only raises it higher. Rather than embracing the standard, he constantly pushes the envelope further with a distinct, robust soundscape all his own.

BIJOU’s show-stopping 2016 collaboration with Dr. Fresch, “Hello” marked a major turning point for his career in music and Future Ghetto as a whole. In the same week, his debut on Night Bass thrust BIJOU to the forefront of the G-House movement and he has never looked back.

His records continue to catch fire, gaining massive support from AC Slater, Destructo, Don Diablo, Drezo, Malaa, Party Favor and many more. BIJOU fed the blaze with a series of ambitious releases including “Gotta Shine” featuring Germ, “Revelation” with Dr. Fresch featuring Denzel Curry, and “Louis V” with modern legend and Night Bass champion AC Slater. BIJOU topped off 2018 with his stellar 4-track Super Phat EP, an instant staple in the modern dance scene. Flash-forward to 2019 and his Gangsta Party EP with Dr. Fresch (DND Records) has primed the producer for yet another successful year.

Infusing elements of hip hop and classic house, BIJOU’s sound is live enough for the underground, but mean enough to hold down any main stage. Fans at EDC Vegas in 2017 witnessed this firsthand as he took over kineticFIELD in full form. He followed up in 2018 with a thrilling Australian run and his first headlining U.S. Super Phat Tour. Having gained all the street cred he needs, BIJOU is now looking worldwide.

Keep your eyes and ears locked on BIJOU — fearless leader, G-House supreme — because he’s about to take over!
