value.title: How old do I have to be to enter SILO?

value.body: SILO is a space for people to dance, to hear music, and to express themselves. While you are here, we want you to feel safe, comfortable, and at home. We do not tolerate violence, harassment, racism, homophobia, transphobia, or bigotry of any kind. We do not allow unwanted contact. This includes leering, staring, and cutting off someone else’s ability to move freely.
value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. Our staff is trained to assist you, so just give them a heads up when you arrive and they will make sure you’re able to get in. Reserved seating can be arranged by emailing a11y@silobrooklyn.com. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible for me?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Oliver Smith has been described as "an excellent DJ" by Armin van Buuren, "the best thing to happen in trance" by Mixmag and "sensational" by DJ Magazine. In recent years the popular UK-based DJ and dance music producer has released scores of records and performed at some of the biggest clubs and festivals in the world.

Oliver’s forward thinking music is regularly played by leading DJs such as Above & Beyond, Hardwell, David Guetta, Ferry Corsten and Sander van Doorn. He was the first signing to the Anjunabeats record label and is the only producer (other than label bosses Above & Beyond) to have featured on all 13 ‘Anjunabeats Volume’ compilations to date. Oliver has also been highly successful with remixes for the likes of Arty, Mat Zo, Seven Lions, and Maor Levi - all featuring on leading radio and club play lists and flying high in the Spotify and Beatport charts. In 2018 he mixed the ‘Anjunabeats Worldwide 08’ compilation, which includes ten of his own productions. It reached the #1 spot on the iTunes dance chart in USA, UK, Canada, Australia and more.

As a DJ, Oliver has played at legendary UK venues such as Ministry of Sound, The Warehouse Project and Wembley Arena; and at far flung locations worldwide including America, India, and Ibiza. He has also performed at some of the biggest festivals in the world such as Tomorrowland, EDC Las Vegas, and Creamfields. He is also a regular presenter of Anjunabeats Worldwide Radio, which is broadcast on over 100 FM stations across the planet.

\--

Genix has deep roots in dance music that have helped his production career to grow exponentially since his debut release in 2003. Since then he has become a mainstay of

Anjunabeats, with other releases on Armada, Vandit Records, Enhanced Records and Spinnin Records to name a few. DJing alongside the world’s elite along the way, he has become a huge name in his own right.

A very successful 2024 saw Genix release his second artist album titled YOU.ME.NOW, a stellar follow up to his debut album ‘199X’ which both led to successful global tour dates around the world from Asia, Australia, Europe & USA. The pick of album tracks were played on BBC radio 1 where Genix went on to host his own show as part of an Anjunabeats takeover.

His formidable sound blends the most vibrant elements of trance, techno, house and progressive into a potent, high octane cocktail. With a penchant for in-your-face textures and sounds set against stunning melody and beautiful atmospherics, his sound is at the vanguard of the trance movement. Blending reverence for the formative sounds of a 1990s dance music upbringing with the sounds of now, his tracks are consistently among the most spinetingling in the scene. With no compromise in his style across his 200+ released singles and remixes, he is an artist who is truly dedicated to his scene. Collaborating with and remixing the likes of Armin van Buuren, Above & Beyond, Gabriel & Dresden and Cosmic Gate, he has become part of the fabric of the scene.

He first found fame as a resident and promoter at legendary UK club night Passion, which was one of the epicentres of the ‘90s/2000s trance explosion. Cutting his name alongside the scene’s biggest DJs, he amassed a wealth of knowledge and experience that would give him solid foundations for the rest of his career. By the time he turned his hand to production in the early 2000s, he had a keen understanding of what worked on a dancefloor, giving him a huge head start. It quickly became clear that he was as talented in the studio as behind the decks, and it wasn’t long before he was attracting major attention.

At one point he held the Guinness World Record for the longest DJ set in history, clocking in at 84 hours. He also recently broke the world record for playing a DJ set at the highest recorded land altitude, playing at Mount Everest Base Camp at 5,600 metres above sea level. He has supported Above & Beyond at epic shows across the world including at the New York Expo Centre, The Gorge Amphitheater in Washington and the O2 Arena Prague and laid waste to some of the world’s biggest dance festivals including Tomorrowland, Creamfields, Dreamstate and A State of Trance.

Lilith Phillips is a songwriter and multi-instrumentalist from Brooklyn, NY. raw.description:
**Emma Ruth Rundle** made a conscious choice to reach towards making a hopeful record for the follow up to 2021’s *Engine of Hell*. Where outside forces tempted her to turn inwards, towards isolation and hopelessness, she instead reached outwards to create a record that acknowledges pain, but offers both community and resilience in response. Although *These Killing Times* possesses a spirit of defiance, it retains the tenderness and vulnerability that saw her earlier work resonate with so many listeners.

*These Killing Times* is electrifying, emotional, and charged with feminine rage; it is a reactive anthology, bristling, full of life and full of resistance - forged by and for community. It asks many questions - of the roles we play as individuals, or as artists - and closes with this one: what will we live for beyond the valley of the shadow of the fear of all men? A question with no definitive answer as yet, but one that is being asked with increasing urgency - here on this record, and beyond.

**Cinder Well** is the musical project of Los Angeles–based songwriter, composer, and multi-instrumentalist Amelia Baker. Cinder Well extracts dark, rich and tender compositions which nod to, but also stray from traditional musical languages.

raw.description:
Deaf Club is a savage sound bath dripping with sardonicism: a blastbeat-centric hardcore punk assault channeling crust, thrash, and grind (un)sensibilities. Succinct pauses, surreal frequencies and effects, breakneck pace and sharply hurled vocals characterize the band’s aesthetic, which seems as though it is rooted in a sort of nasty-sound-meets-highbrow-message ethos. Fueled by the onslaught of society’s insanity and driven mad by tinnitus, Justin Pearson (The Locust, Dead Cross), Brian Amalfitano, Scott Osment (Glassing, Planet B), and Collin Smith approach music as an opportunity to confront our collective sicknesses.

The band initially released their debut EP, Contemporary Sickness, via Three One G in 2019. Having had time to stew in the cesspool of two years of pandemic, and mutating into its newest variant, their debut longplayer, Productive Disruption, dropped in 2022, ventured deeper into the abyss. 2025’s sophomore album, We Demand a Permanent State of Happiness was released on Southern Lord September 2025. Since then the band have been touring regularly across North America and Europe, including an appearance at Roskilde Festival. They have shared stages with Converge, Melt Banana, John Waters, Negative Approach, Napalm Death, Unbroken, and Saetia.

EARLY SHOW ADDED DUE TO DEMAND

**Emma Ruth Rundle** made a conscious choice to reach towards making a hopeful record for the follow up to 2021’s *Engine of Hell*. Where outside forces tempted her to turn inwards, towards isolation and hopelessness, she instead reached outwards to create a record that acknowledges pain, but offers both community and resilience in response. Although *These Killing Times* possesses a spirit of defiance, it retains the tenderness and vulnerability that saw her earlier work resonate with so many listeners.

*These Killing Times* is electrifying, emotional, and charged with feminine rage; it is a reactive anthology, bristling, full of life and full of resistance - forged by and for community. It asks many questions - of the roles we play as individuals, or as artists - and closes with this one: what will we live for beyond the valley of the shadow of the fear of all men? A question with no definitive answer as yet, but one that is being asked with increasing urgency - here on this record, and beyond.

**Cinder Well** is the musical project of Los Angeles–based songwriter, composer, and multi-instrumentalist Amelia Baker. Cinder Well extracts dark, rich and tender compositions which nod to, but also stray from traditional musical languages.

value.body: SILO is a space for people to dance, to hear music, and to express themselves. While you are here, we want you to feel safe, comfortable, and at home. value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
Locky found his love for dance music on London’s dance floors and through its nightlife. That early connection to the energy of the UK underground shaped a sound rooted in house and garage—grounded in tradition but always moving forward. Those who have had the chance to experience a Locky set can attest that the musical journey they undertake is a bit like an ode to London itself. This is down to the thousands of hours Locky has spent on dancefloors across the capital city, soaking up every element of iconic parties from Fuse to Appetite, which he translates across his production and sets.

Since 2019, Locky has evolved from a raver into a world-respected selector. He started off playing parties around his home city at venues like Fabric & 93 Feet East, honing his skills as a DJ. In 2022, Locky burst onto the Underground House scene with an impactful release on Beeyou. He followed with tasteful releases across multiple respected labels such as neXup, UVAR, and many more that garnered support from a long list of industry heavyweights that includes names like Chris Stussy, Rossi, and Enzo Siragusa. 2025 has seen Locky play around the world in countries such as Sri Lanka, Australia, and Spain, at top parties and venues such as The Warehouse Project, After Caposile, and Appetite, to name a few.

Looking forward, Locky has his sights on dominating the global house music market. With massive releases in the pipeline coming alongside his best friends, Max Dean, Luke Dean, and Mad. Again. You’ll find Locky playing the world’s biggest stages, such as Glastonbury, Shelter, and virtually every club in Ibiza, where he’ll be shaping the ears of modern-day ravers, whose shoes he was in not so long ago, one cathartic set at a time.

Watson is also a co founder of Box of Cats, the label launched in 2016 alongside Wongo and fellow producers, giving him another outlet for forward thinking house music.

raw.description:
Pablo Fierro returns to New York on Saturday, December 12th for a late night session at Unveiled, the subterranean club beneath The William Vale in Williamsburg. Joining him is ASMOT, Luna Mar, and KASSIN.

Born and raised in the Canary Islands, Fierro has built a career around the African, Latin, European, and island influences that shaped his musical upbringing. His sets move through Afro house, deep house, percussion, jazz, and soulful club music, creating long stretches of music that develop naturally over the course of the night.

Beyond the booth, Fierro is the founder of Vida Records and the mind behind WE’RE HERE, his label and international event series. The brand has traveled through Morocco, Tunisia, Chicago, Miami, Barcelona, and Ibiza, where it held a residency at Club Chinois. His catalog has also appeared on labels including Innervisions and MoBlack Records.

Gray Area resident Luna Mar brings house, Afro house, Afrotech, and tech house influences shaped by her Puerto Rican roots, while local talents KASSIN and ASMOT complete the bill.

Set beneath The William Vale, Unveiled offers an intimate room, state of the art sound, and a close connection between artist and crowd for a night built to go deep.

On December 12th, MVSON lands at 99 Scott for a New York takeover bringing the Manchester born event brand and record label to Brooklyn.

MVSON grew out of Manchester’s club scene as a platform for parties, music and the community surrounding both. What began through underground events in the city developed into a wider world of club nights and releases, carrying the character of its beginnings into new cities and venues.

MVSON events have become known for carefully selected lineups, packed rooms and crowds that reflect the open spirit at the center of the brand. Rather than operating as a standard artist led party series, MVSON has developed into a platform of its own, bringing together names from across house and club music while creating space for artists connected to its wider circle.

Alongside the events, MVSON has expanded into a record label, giving the platform another way to introduce music beyond the dance floor. The label serves as a home for releases tied to the sound and culture surrounding the parties.

Now MVSON heads to New York, with 99 Scott becoming the next setting for the UK born brand as its event series and label arrive in Brooklyn for one night.

Built from Manchester club culture and carried outward through its events and releases, MVSON has become a meeting point for artists, records and crowds around it. December 12th marks the next step for the platform as it brings that energy into a well known Brooklyn room.

value.body: All of our events are 21+ unless otherwise specified. For 21+ events, all guests must show their government-issued photo identification or passport upon entry.
value.title: How old do I have to be to enter SILO?

value.body: SILO is a space for people to dance, to hear music, and to express themselves. While you are here, we want you to feel safe, comfortable, and at home. We do not tolerate violence, harassment, racism, homophobia, transphobia, or bigotry of any kind. We do not allow unwanted contact. This includes leering, staring, and cutting off someone else’s ability to move freely.
value.title: How does SILO promote a Safer Space?

value.body: If you experience behavior that is threatening or that makes you uncomfortable, please approach a staff member. Our staff is trained to handle these situations, and we will actively remove individuals who make others feel unsafe.
value.title: What if I experience inappropriate behavior from someone?

value.body: All spaces in the venue, including the stage, are accessible to wheelchair users. Our main entrance at 90 Scott Avenue is accessible. Our staff is trained to assist you, so just give them a heads up when you arrive and they will make sure you’re able to get in. Reserved seating can be arranged by emailing a11y@silobrooklyn.com. If you have another accessibility concern, please email a11y@silobrooklyn.com, and we would be happy to see how we can accommodate :)
value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.body: All of our restrooms are gender neutral. There are two accessible stalls, one in each of the two restrooms at the front. If you need any assistance, let a staff member know and they’ll help you out.
value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.
value.title: Transfer your ticket to a friend

value.body: Our ticketed music events have loud music and use strobe lights and haze. If you have allergies or sensitivities to these things, please be aware that we use them in our performances.
value.title: Do you guys use haze/fog?

value.body: There is a water station at the front bar with free water. The bar sells chicken tenders, vegan nuggets, hippeas, and pork rinds.
value.title: I’m kind of hungry and thirsty. What should I do?

value.body: Earplugs are $2 at the front bar.
value.title: Do you sell earplugs?

value.body: All tickets can be found on our Dice.fm page, and all ticket sales are final. If an event is postponed or rescheduled, ticket holders will be able to keep their ticket for the rescheduled date or claim a refund. In the event of a full cancellation, refunds will be processed automatically.
value.title: How do I get tickets at SILO?

value.body: Yes! We sell tickets at the door on a first-come first-serve basis.
value.title: Will there be tickets at the door?

value.body: The front room lounge of SILO is open Wednesday, 8pm-2am for Open Decks and Thursday 9pm-3am, usually for a DJ event with a local collective. Open Decks and most Thursday events are free as long as you RSVP ahead of time on Dice. Once a month or so we have a free-with-RSVP weekend event.
value.title: Do you only have ticketed events?

value.body: We usually allow re-entry, but for sold out shows exits may be final if we are at capacity.
value.title: Are exits final? What if I gotta step out for a second?

value.body: There is a designated smoking area just outside the side door to the right of the stage. There will be a member of our security team at the door who will check your stamp upon re-entering the venue.
value.title: What if I want to have a smoke?

value.body: Yes! Each item is $5, cash or card.

Deeper Purpose is the house and tech house project of London born DJ and producer Stephen Galloway who has become a renowned name on the global club and festival circuit. His infectious house records have landed on labels like Catch and Release Toolroom Experts Only Insomniac and more including a breakout Beatport topping remix of Piero Pirupa Everybody’s Free To Feel Good which became the platforms longest running tech house number one in 2021.

In 2024 he launched his label In 2 Deep and took it across North America on his biggest headline run to date confirming his place as a leading voice in the new wave of tech house.

On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

value.title: I’m a wheelchair user and want to experience a night at SILO. How do you make it accessible?

value.title: What about restrooms?

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

Live aerialists, immersive visuals, and a champagne toast and balloon drop at midnight!  
  
Gravagerz is an Italian DJ, record producer, and songwriter based in Luxembourg. Known for his signature Euphoric House sound, he blends elements of House, UK Garage, and Dubstep into his productions. As an independent artist, Gravagerz has accumulated over 7 million monthly Spotify listeners and more than 300 million combined streams across various platforms. In addition to his solo work, he is a versatile producer, collaborating with hip-hop, pop, K-pop, R&B, and dance artists on their upcoming albums.

In 2020, Gravagerz signed a management contract with Leaf Music Management at the age of 17. His early releases included "Look Back at It" with Tom Field on B1 Recordings, as well as remixes for Regard x Ella Henderson and Era Istrefi. His breakthrough came with "Chihiro", originally a remix of Billie Eilish's song on SoundCloud, which went viral on TikTok and Instagram, amassing over 200 million combined streams and 1.2 million video creators using the track. After replacing the vocals, he officially released it as his own version.  
  
Following this success, he secured an official remix of Quavo and Lana Del Rey’s “Tough” followed by another official cover release of Disclosure and London Grammar’s “Help Me Lose My Mind”, which garnered over 50 million streams and 50,000 video creators on social media.

In April 2025, Gravagerz released “Pool” featuring Kiki Wera, marking his first record to chart in the UK Top 100, reaching 15 million combined streams and inspiring 20,000 video creators.

His remixes frequently go viral on TikTok, with multiple tracks exceeding 50,000 video creators, including Drake’s “Time Flies,” A$AP Rocky’s “Fukk Sleep,” and WizzTheMC’s “Show Me Love."

Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.

value.body:
On the day of the event (usually 2h before it starts) you’ll be able to activate your ticket in the app and generate your unique QR code.

Just follow these steps.

1\. Open the DICE app. Tap the ticket icon at the bottom of the screen.

2\. Choose the event.

3\. Tap Activate QR code.

Once you activate your ticket, you will no longer be able to send it to a friend.

If you bought tickets for a group and you’re arriving together, you can show everyone’s tickets on your device to the door staff.
value.title: What do I do on the day of the event?

value.body:
Offer your ticket to another fan

We believe tickets belong in the hands of fans, and that they should only ever be sold for a fair price. That’s why we have the Waiting List: if you can’t make it to a sold-out event, you can add your ticket to the queue to be purchased by another fan. If the ticket is sold, you’ll get your money back – no drama, no rip-offs.

There are a few conditions, though. Not every show will have the Waiting List function switched on (that’s up to the event organisers, not DICE), and tickets can only be added to the Waiting List after a show sells out. On top of that – and this is important – you’ll only get your money back if another fan buys your ticket.
value.title: What if I can’t make the event anymore?

value.body:
If a friend is keen to attend an event you can’t make, you can transfer your ticket to them quickly and securely within the app. Just make sure you have their number saved in your phone, and that they have a DICE account registered with that number.

After you transfer the ticket, it will be stored within the DICE app on your friend’s phone – there’s no fiddling with name changes, emailing PDFs, or sending across screenshots. It’s just another way we make sure tickets don’t fall into the wrong hands.

raw.description:
ØTTA takes over The Roof, bringing her mix of Brazilian trance, techno, psytrance, hard house, and UK garage influences to New York.

The Brazilian artist first gained wider attention through releases including the Plus One EP and Candy22, pairing old school psytrance with Brazilian drums, rolling basslines, bright melodies, and unexpected vocals. Her first Boiler Room performance marked a major point in her rise, introducing audiences around the world to a set style that moves freely between faster club sounds.

In 2024, she released the four track In My 2024 Era EP and launched Hotties, her own record label and event series. The platform has since grown into an outlet for new music and parties featuring artists from across the international club circuit. She followed in 2025 with “Mão Na Parede,” released through Boys Noize’s One To Zero project.

Her 2026 schedule has included Awakenings, Love Family Park, WECANDANCE, Audioriver, Lovefest, Boothstock, RSO.BERLIN, Hï Ibiza, and Brunch Electronik Lisboa. She also returned to New York for Boiler Room beneath the K Bridge.

Now developing a new album while spending time in Rio de Janeiro, ØTTA arrives at Chocolate Factory with new music taking shape and another full year of international shows behind her.
